..FOR EXTREME SOUTHWESTERN CALIFORNIA INCLUDING ORANGE...
SAN DIEGO...WESTERN RIVERSIDE AND SOUTHWESTERN SAN BERNARDINO
COUNTIES...

Today through tomorrow night...

The latest satellite imagery at midnight reveals that the marine 
layer continues to struggle over the inner socal bight waters, 
thanks partially in part to an eddy that has developed near Catalina 
and has helped to create a stronger offshore flow for San Diego 
County as a result. This is also helping to erode some of the marine 
layer that has already developed over Orange County, as SE'ly 
surface winds have picked up due to the coastal eddy. There will 
still likely be some additional low cloud development, and skies may 
periodically go broken right along the coastal areas through this 
morning, with ceilings hovering around 1000 ft MSL. Otherwise, 
mostly clear skies will prevail and set up for another very warm day 
with temperatures still running generally around 5 to 10 degrees 
above the average for this time of year. There has also been some 
recycled mid-level monsoonal moisture that has been streaming over 
the region this morning, which may allow for a very slight chance of 
a shower or two to develop over the mountains (likely only confined 
to the highest elevations), although confidence is low given the 
lack of instability over the region. Hi-res guidance also does not 
suggest much in the way of development later on, although given that 
there is some moisture present, and a monsoonal wave transitioning 
towards the area, which may help to destabilize the mid-levels later 
on, a possible shower or two cannot be ruled out. However, it is a 
lot less likely with very little instability aloft that these would 
become thunderstorms. Under a strengthening ridge, highs will still 
be running around 5 to 10 degrees above the seasonal average for 
this time of year for today.

By tomorrow, winds in the mid-levels will begin to shift to become 
more southwesterly, and draw in drier air along with it. This will 
help to impede the chance of afternoon shower and thunderstorm 
development over the mountains. The troughing upstream will also 
begin to influence the area with slightly lower heights that will 
begin a gradual cooling trend beginning tomorrow. There will also 
begin the presence of a more predominant onshore flow, and this will 
likely help to draw in the marine layer a little sooner, and with 
better coverage for the following night. In addition, this is also 
going to allow for winds to increase through San Gorgonio Pass, and 
along the desert slopes, with gusts up around 40 mph through the 
early evening. This will continue to likely be the case through 
Wednesday as stronger onshore flow remains in place.

Monday through Friday...

Subtle cooling will continue through the mid half of next week and 
conditions will remain dry, with temperatures still being above 
average. Thereafter, mid-level winds will begin to shift back to 
being from a more easterly direction, with better positioning of the 
high pressure center aloft to allow for some of these monsoonal 
waves to develop and advect moisture over our region. Temperatures 
will also start to gradually warm again during this period, with 
increased humidity values and an increasing chance of getting 
thunderstorm activity for our mountains and deserts (and possibly 
even all the way to the coastal locations, depending on the 
propagation of these monsoonal waves as they develop over the 
deserts to our southeast and then transition over our region. During 
this period, the marine layer will likely struggle to develop, given 
the increased mid to high level clouds moving overhead, in
addition, with better offshore flow overnight.
